message.content:
This is the key. `AddNameData` uses `realloc` on `namedata`. When `realloc` shifts the buffer, pointers previously returned (like `xmlbase = &namedata[index]` and `uri = &namedata[index]`) become dangling. 

The bug: In `ProcessSsmlTag`, `xmlbase` is set to `&namedata[index]` (line 895). Then later, when another `AddNameData` call reallocates `namedata`, the `xmlbase` pointer becomes stale (use-after-free). Then `xmlbase` is used at line 820: `sprintf(fname, "%s/%s", xmlbase, buf)`.

Let me look at how `xmlbase` is passed and used across the parsing loop. Let me find the main SSML parsing loop.
